result.title: Best Arm Identification with Unknown Post-Action Context Distribution
result.summary: We study best arm identification (BAI) with post-action context in the fixed-confidence setting. After choosing an action, the learner observes a post-action context together with a reward whose distribution depends only on this context. Incorporating such intermediate information can substantially reduce the sample complexity of identifying the best arm. While Shahverdikondori et al. (2026a) analyzed the case where the distribution of contexts given actions is known, we address the more challenging and practically relevant case where this distribution is unknown. We derive an instance-dependent sample complexity lower bound and propose a Track-and-Stop algorithm that matches it asymptotically with access to an optimization oracle. Our stopping rule uses a new concentration inequality that jointly controls uncertainty in the context distributions and reward means, removing the factor of two incurred by separate concentration bounds. Implementing the algorithm generally requires solving nonconvex optimization problems. We propose a convex relaxation with instance-dependent approximation guarantees, including asymptotic tightness on hard Gaussian instances. Experiments demonstrate that exploiting post-action context reduces the sample complexity relative to baselines that ignore it, even when the context distributions are unknown.

AI.brief_summary: 研究动作后上下文分布未知情形下的固定置信度最佳臂识别，给出实例相关的样本复杂度下界，并提出 Track-and-Stop 算法、联合控制上下文分布与奖励均值不确定性的浓度不等式，以及带近似保证的凸松弛。
AI.relevance_reason: 其自适应采样、基于置信界的停止规则与「中间证据降低样本成本」的形式化分析，可能为 LVR 中何时继续获取视觉证据、何时停止的计算—证据权衡提供可核查的理论框架，但领域距离较远。
